sections.html:
The Clay County Recorder of Deeds files deeds, deeds of trust, plats, surveys, powers of attorney and tax liens. The office is in the Administration building at 1 Courthouse Square in Liberty, with mail going to PO Box 238, Liberty, MO 64069. Staff can be reached at 816-407-3550 or recorder@claycountymo.gov.

The counter is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., but nothing is recorded and no marriage license issued once 4:00 p.m. passes. Get a deed signed late in the day to the office before that cutoff, and ask your title company how it will be delivered. There is no recorder location at the Annex, so use the courthouse square address.

Deciding what needs recording is not the office's job. Staff check that a document meets state requirements and then preserve it as a permanent public record.

Plan on $26.00 for page one of a standard document and $3.00 for each page after it. The office takes cash, check and credit card, and the card processor adds its own fee. A statewide change on August 28, 2026 added a flat $2.00 to recording charges, so a fee sheet saved before then understates the cost.

Military discharges are recorded at no charge. The state side of the charge sits in RSMo 59.319, which sets a six dollar user fee on every recorded instrument on top of other fees, and three dollars of it stays with the recorder in a fund for record storage and preservation. A long document is priced page by page, so phone the office with the page count first.

sections.h2: Format rules that can get a deed refused
sections.html:
RSMo 59.310 lets the recorder refuse a document that misses its format rules, or record it as a non-standard document for the extra $25.00. The county's document standards page spells out the details.

  • Letter size sheets, white or light colored, 20 pound stock, with no watermark or logo and print on a single side.
  • Dark ink throughout, text of at least 8 point, and a typed, stamped or printed name beneath every signature.
  • Three blank inches across the top of page one and three quarters of an inch on the remaining margins.
  • Page one must carry the title, date, every grantor with marital status, every grantee, statutory addresses, the legal description and any book and page reference.

The county asks for the full legal description and says it should not be copied from tax bills. Exempt from the standardization rules are documents signed before January 1, 2002, military separation papers, papers executed abroad, certified copies and court judgments. A rejected document comes back with the reason written out.

sections.h2: How to find or copy a recorded deed
sections.html:
Online records live on the iCounty portal at claymo.icounty.com. Register as a user to view images at no charge, while copies must be bought. For subscription questions, call iCounty at (816) 295-1540. The recorder's own line, 816-407-3550, handles everything else.

Records are indexed by name, so a search by street address will not work. The office recommends a property printout from the Clay County Assessor's real estate division, which gives the deed's book and page and speeds up a copy request. Online records run from 1968 to the present. Deeds were hand recorded in books from 1822 until an automated database began in 1986, and imaging of daily records started in August 1999.

Copies run $2.00 for page one and $1.00 for later pages, with certification at $1.00 per document. Orders paid by card can be emailed or mailed to you.

sections.h2: What the recorder will not do
sections.html:
State statute bars the office from searching for liens or saying whether one exists. Use the public computer at the office or hire a title company to run the search. A recorded deed also stays as it is. Adding or removing a name takes a new deed, prepared and recorded at the going rate.

  • Sale prices: these are not public record here, though the Assessor may give you the area's market value.
  • Building details: the files describe land, so the Assessor is the place to ask when improvements were added.
  • Blank forms: staff cannot draft legal documents, so a quit claim or warranty deed comes from you or an attorney.
  • Foreclosure lists: look for notices in the Kearney Courier or the Excelsior Springs Daily Standard and call the named trustee.

Paying off a mortgage records a release of the deed of trust. A release is not proof of ownership, since the deed from your seller is the document that shows you own the home. The county also runs Deed Watch, a free email alert at deedwatch.com that tells you when a document is recorded under a name you choose.

Clay County is part of the Kansas City metro area, with the northern suburbs and part of Kansas City itself inside its lines. The July 2025 estimate is 265,032 residents and 110,443 housing units. Owners occupy 69.5% of homes, the owner-occupied median value over 2020 to 2024 is $275,600 and median household income is $88,468. Renters pay a median $1,243, and 297 building permits were issued in 2025.

Whatever town your house is in, whether Liberty, Gladstone, Kearney, Smithville or North Kansas City, the same Liberty office files the deed. Ask the closing attorney or title company who will deliver it, so it arrives ahead of the 4:00 p.m. cutoff.

faqs.q: What does Clay County charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: $26.00 for page one and $3.00 for each added page, with $25.00 more for a non-standard document. These amounts include the flat $2.00 statewide increase effective August 28, 2026. Confirm page counts and card fees at 816-407-3550.

faqs.q: Until what time can a deed be filed?
faqs.a: Until 4:00 p.m. on weekdays. The office stays open to 5:00 p.m. but takes no recordings after 4:00. It is at 1 Courthouse Square in Liberty, with a PO Box 238 mailing address.

faqs.q: Can I search a deed by street address?
faqs.a: No. Records are indexed by name, not location. Get the book and page from the Clay County Assessor's real estate division, then use the recorder's online search or call the office. Online viewing is free once you register, while copies are paid.

faqs.q: Can the recorder fix a name or legal description on a deed that is already recorded?
faqs.a: No. A recorded document is a permanent record and cannot be edited. To change the title, a new deed or corrective document has to be prepared by you or an attorney and recorded at the current fee.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax line on the fee schedule?
faqs.a: The schedule lists recording, copy, certification, plat, lien and marriage license charges, and no transfer tax. Ask the Recorder at 816-407-3550 or your title company about any other cost tied to a particular closing.
